_note: Values that encode a DECISION rather than a measurement. tools/check-decisions.py recomputes each from its own real source and REFUSES if one has moved, because a decision changing is exactly the case where a deliberate act should be required — and editing this file in the same commit is that act. The other thirty-odd numbers this build prints move every run for good reasons; these do not. Shape taken from the D'Arcy session's decisions.json, machinery from the kit.

kitPin.why: Which build of the shared kit this archive's gates are. In the D'Arcy archive this moved inside a commit about gating a chart and three builds printed the correct new value under «ok» before anybody read it.

livingPolicy.why: A living person is named and nothing else about them is published — David's rule. Read from the check:living script itself, so changing the flag in package.json is what this catches.

kinRatchet.why: No relationship in this archive is impossible, and that number may only go down. Read from the check:kin script's --max, so loosening the ratchet is a visible act rather than a quiet one.

namedLiving.why: The one living person this archive names, and she is named because she is a SOURCE: the Anglo-Boer War account and the name-change come from her testimony as told by her father. Recorded b = "living", with no flag anywhere — which is why the living gate counted zero here until 27 September 2026. Anyone appearing or disappearing from this list is a change to who this archive publishes. As of 31f7a5c the vocabulary that finds her is declared in kit/data/living-words.json and read by both the gate and /register, because three separate readers of "is this person alive" had each missed her in a different way.
